report.source_text: A muscle biopsy from the left rectus femoris revealed histological findings reflecting active muscle fiber necrosis and regenerative changes (Fig. 2). Reactive mononuclear cell infiltration was seen surrounding necrotic and regenerating fibers. Immunostaining showed the expression of human leukocyte antigen (HLA)-ABC and deposition of membrane attack complex (MAC) on the muscle fiber membranes. Perifascicular atrophy, fibers with internal nuclei, and endomysial fibrosis were not seen. No perivascular collections of inflammatory cells were apparent.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Inflammatory myopathy with clinical classification of polymyositis (PM)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 69-year-old Japanese woman presented with a 3-year history of unexplained weight loss and several months of progressive mild muscle weakness affecting the neck and symmetrical proximal upper and lower limbs with mild atrophy, but without dermatomyositis skin features (no Gottron's lesion, heliotrope rash, mechanic's hands, or sclerosis). Initial laboratory workup on admission revealed elevated muscle enzymes (CK 1,081 IU/L, aldolase 12.7 IU/L) and systemic inflammation (ESR 50.9 mm/h, CRP 4.76 mg/dL), with elevated KL-6 (589 IU/mL) suggesting possible pulmonary involvement. Needle electromyography demonstrated a myopathic pattern with early recruitment and small amplitude motor units. Muscle biopsy from the left rectus femoris showed active muscle fiber necrosis with regenerative changes and reactive mononuclear cell infiltration surrounding necrotic and regenerating fibers, with HLA-ABC and MAC deposition on fiber membranes, but notably absent perifascicular atrophy, perivascular inflammation, and endomysial fibrosis—findings consistent with polymyositis rather than dermatomyositis. Myositis-specific antibody testing was negative for anti-Jo-1, anti-Mi-2, anti-SRP, and anti-HMGCR, but positive for anti-centromere and anti-PM/Scl-75 antibodies. Chest CT revealed mild interstitial changes at the base of the lower lung fields bilaterally, consistent with myositis-associated interstitial lung disease. The patient was treated with oral prednisolone 40 mg/day (1 mg/kg/day) with gradual improvement in muscle weakness and normalization of CK to 211 U/L at discharge.
